definition_zh: 年龄；岁数；老年；时代；使用年限
definition_en: the number of years a person or thing has existed, or a period of history, or the state of being old
core_image: 墙上每年添一支蜡烛，火苗越积越高，照亮一段又一段年月
scene: 老宅的墙边排着一排旧木箱，每个箱面都刻着年份。As the years passed, the age of the house showed in its cracked walls.
sceneCN: 这里 age 是「使用年限、年头」（第 4 个义项：器物已经存在的时长）；句意为随着年月流逝，这所房子的年头从开裂的墙上显了出来。

pos.zh: 名词：年龄；时代；老年；使用年限
动词：变老；使显老

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ed 构成，义为「年老的；年久的」
由本词加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「变老；老化」
由本词加后缀 -less 构成，义为「不显老的；永恒的」
由本词加后缀 -ism 构成，义为「年龄歧视」

senses.title: How many years someone has lived
senses.definition: the number of years a person or animal has lived
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物已经活过的年数
senses.example: She learned to swim at the age of five.
senses.exampleCN: 她五岁学会了游泳。
senses.why: Latin aetas first meant a span of life, so counting the years lived is the most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aetas 最初指「一生的跨度」，所以数出活过的年数是最本义的用法。

senses.title: The state of being old
senses.definition: the later part of life, when a person or thing has existed for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 生命的后期，人或物已经存在很久的阶段
senses.example: His face showed the quiet marks of age.
senses.exampleCN: 他的脸上留着岁月安静的痕迹。
senses.why: Because aetas covers the whole span of life, its far end naturally names old age itself.
senses.whyCN: 既然 aetas 覆盖整段生命跨度，这段跨度的末端自然就用来指老年本身。

senses.title: A period of history
senses.definition: a particular period in history, often named after a person or a feature
senses.definitionCN: 历史上的一段时期，常以人物或特征命名
senses.example: The museum collects tools from the Stone Age.
senses.exampleCN: 这座博物馆收藏石器时代的工具。
senses.why: A human lifetime became the model for any long stretch of time, so whole eras are called ages.
senses.whyCN: 人的一生被当作任何长时间段的模型，于是整个历史阶段也被称为 age。

senses.title: How long something has been in use
senses.definition: the length of time a machine, building, or object has existed or can be used
senses.definitionCN: 机器、建筑或器物已经存在或还能使用的时长
senses.example: The age of the bridge was clear from the worn stone.
senses.exampleCN: 从磨损的石块就能看出这座桥的年头。
senses.why: The lifespan image moves easily from people to objects, which also have a span of service.
senses.whyCN: 「寿命」的意象很容易从人转到器物，器物同样有一段服役的时长。

senses.title: A very long time, informally
senses.definition: a long period, used in the plural in informal speech, as in for ages
senses.definitionCN: 很长一段时间，口语中常用复数，如 for ages
senses.example: I have not seen her for ages.
senses.exampleCN: 我很久没见过她了。
senses.why: The word for a whole lifetime is stretched hyperbolically to mean any long wait.
senses.whyCN: 表示「一生」的词被夸张地拉长，用来指任何漫长的等待。

senses.title: To grow old
senses.definition: to become older or to show the effects of getting older
senses.definitionCN: 年龄增长，或显出变老的迹象
senses.example: He aged quickly after the long illness.
senses.exampleCN: 久病之后他老得很快。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into a process: passing through the years that aetas measures.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成过程：走过 aetas 所计量的那些年月。

senses.title: To make someone look old
senses.definition: to make a person or thing look or seem older than they are
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物看起来比实际更老
senses.example: The harsh light aged her face in the photograph.
senses.exampleCN: 刺眼的光线让照片里她的脸显得苍老。
senses.why: This is the causative use: something adds the years that age normally brings.
senses.whyCN: 这是使役用法：某物把 age 本该带来的年岁加到了外表上。

senses.title: A short unit of geological time
senses.definition: a subdivision of geological time shorter than an epoch
senses.definitionCN: 地质时间的划分单位，比世（epoch）更短
senses.example: The rock layer was dated to the late Jurassic age.
senses.exampleCN: 这层岩石被测定为侏罗纪晚期。
senses.why: Geology needed a neutral word for deep time and borrowed the everyday span word.
senses.whyCN: 地质学需要一个指深远时间的中性词，于是借用了日常表示时段的词。

intro.en: Age comes from Latin through Old French, and the family gathers around the idea of a span of life.
intro.cn: age 经由古法语来自拉丁语，整个词族都围绕「一段生命的跨度」这一观念。

items.en: *aiw- is generally reconstructed as meaning vital force or a long life; the deeper origin of this root is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *aiw- 表示「生命力、长久的生命」；这个更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Aevum meant a lifetime or an eternity, and it stands behind the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 aevum 意为「一生、永恒」，是整个词族的源头。

items.en: Aetas, from aetat-, meant a lifetime, a period of life, or an age of the world.
items.cn: 拉丁语 aetas（词干 aetat-）意为「一生、人生阶段、世代的时期」。

items.en: Old French aage carried the word into English with the sense of age or lifetime.
items.cn: 古法语 aage 把这个词带进英语，当时意为「年龄、一生」。

items.en: The noun is recorded in the fourteenth century; the verb to age is much later, from the eighteenth century. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词在十四世纪已有记录；动词用法要晚得多，见于十八世纪。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense spread from people to historical periods and then to the service life of objects and machines.
items.cn: 词义从人扩展到历史时期，再扩展到器物与机器的使用年限。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the same lexical family plus one word that only looks similar; the near-meaning group holds words for periods and spans of time.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族的成员，另加一个只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示时段与生命跨度的词。

entries.definition: An adjective describing someone or something that is old.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「年老的、年久的」，由本词加后缀构成。

entries.definition: The noun or adjective for the process of growing older.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「变老、老化」，指变老的过程。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning never looking old or never ending.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不显老的、永恒的」，由本词加后缀 -less 构成。

entries.definition: An organization that acts for others; it only looks similar, coming from the verb agere rather than from aetas.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代理机构」；只是拼写相近，其词源是动词 agere，与表示生命的 aetas 不同。

entries.definition: A long and distinct period of history, often named for an event or a style.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「时代、纪元」，指历史上长久而独特的一段，常以事件或风格命名。

entries.definition: Any length of time, from minutes to centuries, with a clear beginning and end.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「时期、期间」，可长可短，强调有始有终。

entries.definition: A period that marks a new stage in history or in someone's life.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「新纪元、重大阶段」，强调标志新阶段的时段。

entries.definition: The whole span of one person's life, which is the core image behind age.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一生、寿命」，正是 age 的核心意象。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Aetas is a lifetime, so age at first means the span of years someone has lived.
normal.cn: aetas 指一生，所以 age 最初指一个人活过的那段年月。

normal.en: The same root gives aevum and the adjective aeternus, both about long stretches of time.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 aevum 与形容词 aeternus，都与漫长的时间有关。

normal.en: At the age of is the standard phrase for naming the year something happened.
normal.cn: at the age of 是说明某事发生在几岁时的标准搭配。

normal.en: Come of age means reaching the age when one is treated as an adult.
normal.cn: come of age 意为到了被当作成年人的年龄。

normal.en: The verb to age describes the process, while the noun names the result.
normal.cn: 动词 age 描述过程，名词则指这个过程的结果。

abstract.en: Picture a wall with one candle added every year: the row of flames is a life being counted.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙，每年添一支蜡烛：那一排火苗就是被数出来的一生。

abstract.en: The same row can be read backwards as history: each burnt stub is a period that has passed.
abstract.cn: 同一排蜡烛也可以倒着读成历史：每一截烧剩的蜡都是一个已经过去的时期。

abstract.en: When the wall is full, the last candles stand for old age, and the years left are few.
abstract.cn: 墙插满时，最后几支蜡烛就是老年，剩下的年头已经不多。

examples.en: She learned to swim at the age of five.
examples.cn: 她五岁学会了游泳。

examples.en: The Stone Age tools were made of flint.
examples.cn: 石器时代的工具是用燧石打制的。

examples.en: He aged quickly after the long illness.
examples.cn: 久病之后他老得很快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶举」——问一句几岁，答一个年岁：年龄、岁数

root: 拉丁语 aevum「一生、永恒」衍生出 aetas「一生、人生阶段」，经古法语 aage 进入英语。词族里的 aged、aging、ageless 都由英语后缀扩展而来；原始印欧语 *aiw-「生命力」一般认为成立，更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The senses all grow from one image, a measured span of life: the count of years, the last years, the scale of history, the life of an object, a long wait, and the process of growing old.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项都从同一个意象长出来，即一段被计量的生命：年数、晚年、历史的尺度、器物的寿命、漫长的等待，以及变老的过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one candle is added to the wall every year, and the growing row of flames marks the passing years.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上每年添一支蜡烛，越来越长的一排火苗标出流逝的年月。

branches.en: THE COUNT: aetas is the span of life, so the years lived become a number.
branches.cn: 计数线：aetas 指一生的跨度，活过的年数因此变成一个数字。

branches.en: THE FAR END: the last part of that span is old age itself.
branches.cn: 末端线：这段跨度的最后一段就是老年本身。

branches.en: THE SCALE: one lifetime becomes the model for historical periods and for units of geological time.
branches.cn: 尺度线：一生被当作模型，用来指历史时期与地质时间单位。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: machines and buildings also have a span of service.
branches.cn: 器物线：机器与建筑同样有一段服役的时长。

branches.en: THE STRETCH: a whole lifetime can mean a very long wait, and the verb names passing through the years.
branches.cn: 延展线：一整段生命可以指漫长的等待，动词则指走过这些年月。

intro.en: Age has no living prefix; its structure is a Latin root plus the suffixes that English adds to build the family.
intro.cn: age 没有仍在使用的词缀前缀，它的结构是拉丁词根加上英语用来构词的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Aevum and aetas are both recorded in Latin, so only the older Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 aevum 与 aetas 均有文献记录，只有更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.exampleCN: aevum 是这个词族有记录的最早成员。

items.example: Aetas gave the French and English forms of age.
items.exampleCN: aetas 衍生出法语与英语的 age 形式。

items.example: Old French aage is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 aage 是英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: They argued over an age-old question.

definition_zh: 代理机构；中介；政府机构；能动性；通讯社
definition_en: an organization that acts for others, or the capacity of a person to act independently
core_image: 一只戴着手套的手，替另一只手去按按钮
scene: 街角的小门面只挂着几行字，进门的人把材料交给柜台。She found the flat through a local letting agency.
sceneCN: 这里 agency 是「代理服务机构」（第 1 个义项：替他人提供服务的机构）；句意为她通过当地一家房屋中介找到了这套公寓。

pos.zh: 名词：代理机构；政府机构；能动性

collocations.zh: 自由球员身份；自主行动权

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ial 构成，义为「代理的；能动性的」
由前缀 inter- 加本词构成，义为「跨机构的；机构之间的」
由前缀 sub- 加本词构成，义为「分代理处；下属机构」

senses.title: A business that provides a service
senses.definition: a company that provides a particular service for other people or companies
senses.definitionCN: 替他人或其他公司提供特定服务的机构
senses.example: She found the flat through a local letting agency.
senses.exampleCN: 她通过当地一家房屋中介找到了这套公寓。
senses.why: Latin agentia named the activity of an agent, and the office where that activity is done took over the name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 agentia 指代理人的活动，进行这项活动的办事场所后来沿用了这个名字。

senses.title: A government department
senses.definition: an official organization, especially in the United States, that is part of the government
senses.definitionCN: 官方的组织机构，尤指美国政府部门
senses.example: The environmental agency issued new rules on waste water.
senses.exampleCN: 环保机构发布了新的废水规定。
senses.why: Public bodies act on behalf of the state, so the same word covers official acting for others.
senses.whyCN: 公共机构代表国家行事，于是同一个词也覆盖官方的「代行」关系。

senses.title: The capacity to act
senses.definition: the ability of a person or group to act independently and make their own choices
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体独立行动并自主选择的能力
senses.example: The study asks how much agency workers have over their own hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究追问工人对自己的工时有多少自主权。
senses.why: The abstract sense keeps the core meaning of agere, to act, and names the power behind action.
senses.whyCN: 这一抽象义保留了 agere「行动」的核心，指行动背后的那种能力。

senses.title: Acting through another
senses.definition: the state of one thing acting for another, often in the phrase through the agency of
senses.definitionCN: 一物替另一物起作用的关系，常见于 through the agency of 这一短语
senses.example: The treaty was signed through the agency of a neutral envoy.
senses.exampleCN: 这份条约借助一位中立使者的斡旋得以签署。
senses.why: If an agent does the work, the connection it provides becomes a means or channel.
senses.whyCN: 既然由代理人办事，它提供的这层连接就成了手段或渠道。

senses.title: A news organization
senses.definition: an organization that gathers news and supplies reports to newspapers, websites, and broadcasters
senses.definitionCN: 采集新闻并向报纸、网站和广播机构供稿的组织
senses.example: The story was first reported by a foreign news agency.
senses.exampleCN: 这条消息最早由一家外国通讯社报道。
senses.why: It acts for many outlets at once, collecting what each of them would otherwise gather alone.
senses.whyCN: 它同时替许多媒体办事，采集各媒体本来要各自去跑的消息。

intro.en: Agency is built on the Latin verb agere, to do or drive, and reached English through Old French.
intro.cn: agency 建立在拉丁语动词 agere「做、驱动」之上，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Agere meant to do, to drive, or to act, and it is one of the busiest verbs in Latin.
items.cn: 拉丁语 agere 意为「做、驱动、行动」，是拉丁语中使用极广的动词之一。

items.en: The present participle stem agent- named the one who acts or the thing that acts.
items.cn: 现在分词词干 agent- 指「正在行动的人或物」。

items.en: Agentia meant activity or efficacy, and in later use it also named an office or a deputed function.
items.cn: agentia 意为「活动、效力」，后期也指职位或受托的职能。

items.en: Old French agence carried the word into English with the sense of action or effect.
items.cn: 古法语 agence 把这个词带进英语，当时意为「行动、效果」。

items.en: The word is recorded in the fifteenth century as action or effect; the commercial sense of a business acting for clients appears in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 这个词在十五世纪已有记录，意为「行动、效果」；指替客户办事的商业机构义到十九世纪才出现。

items.en: The government agency sense grew in the twentieth century, and the abstract sense of human agency came from philosophy and sociology.
items.cn: 政府机构义在二十世纪扩展，而「人的能动性」这一抽象义来自哲学与社会学。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the agere family; the near-meaning group gathers organizations and offices that act for others.
note.cn: 形近组收 agere 词族的成员；近义组收替他人行事的各种组织与机构。

entries.definition: One who acts for another, built directly on the same Latin participle stem.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代理人」，直接建立在同一拉丁分词词干上。

entries.definition: The list of things to be done, from the gerundive of the same verb agere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「议程」，来自同一动词 agere 的动形词，字面是「要做的事」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to an agent or to the power to act.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「代理人的、能动性的」，由本词加后缀构成。

entries.definition: A government office or department, often with a specific function.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「局、处」，指有特定职能的政府办事机构。

entries.definition: A group of people working together for a purpose; the widest of these words.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「组织」，范围最宽，指为一项目标而共同工作的群体。

entries.definition: An established body such as a bank, school, or hospital.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「机构、制度性组织」，如银行、学校或医院。

entries.definition: A division of a large organization or government, with its own duties.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部门、司、处」，指大机构或政府中分管事务的单位。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin verb behind the word and the phrases it actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这个词背后的拉丁动词，以及它实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Agere means to act, so an agency is a place where acting for others happens.
normal.cn: agere 意为「行动」，所以 agency 就是替别人行动的地方。

normal.en: Agent, agenda and agency share one root: the doer, the things to do, and the office that does them.
normal.cn: agent、agenda 与 agency 同出一根：做事的人、要做的事、办事的机构。

normal.en: Through the agency of means by the action or help of someone.
normal.cn: through the agency of 意为借助某人的作用或帮助。

normal.en: A news agency collects stories and sells them to many outlets at once.
normal.cn: news agency 采集新闻，同时卖给多家媒体。

normal.en: Human agency is the plain power to choose and act, with no office involved.
normal.cn: human agency 指选择与行动的纯能力，与任何机构无关。

abstract.en: Picture a gloved hand pressing a button for another hand: that is an agent acting in place of someone.
abstract.cn: 想象一只戴着手套的手替另一只手按按钮：这就是代理人代替别人行动。

abstract.en: The glove can be a company, a government office, or an invisible social force.
abstract.cn: 这只手套可以是一家公司、一个政府机构，也可以是一股看不见的社会力量。

abstract.en: Remove the glove and only the power to act remains: that is agency in its abstract sense.
abstract.cn: 把这只手套拿掉，只剩下行动的能力：这就是抽象意义上的 agency。

examples.en: The environmental agency issued new rules on waste water.
examples.cn: 环保机构发布了新的废水规定。

examples.en: The treaty was signed through the agency of a neutral envoy.
examples.cn: 这份条约借助一位中立使者的斡旋得以签署。

examples.en: She found the flat through a local letting agency.
examples.cn: 她通过当地一家房屋中介找到了这套公寓。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶，办事」——替人办事的地方：代理机构

root: 拉丁语 agere「做、驱动」的现在分词词干 agent- 加上名词后缀 -ia 构成 agentia「作用、办事能力」，经古法语 agence 进入英语，由「行动」扩展为「办事机构」，再由哲学用法扩展出「能动性」。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses share one idea, acting in place of someone: a service business, a government office, the plain power to act, the channel through which help comes, and an organization that gathers news for others.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项共享一个观念，即替别人行动：服务性的机构、政府办事部门、行动本身的能力、帮助借以传递的渠道，以及替众多媒体采集新闻的组织。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gloved hand presses a button on behalf of another hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只戴着手套的手替另一只手按下按钮。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: the place where acting for clients is the business itself.
branches.cn: 机构线：替客户办事本身就是业务的场所。

branches.en: THE STATE: an official body acts for the public and carries the same name.
branches.cn: 国家线：官方机构替公众行事，也沿用同一个名字。

branches.en: THE POWER: the abstract sense names the capacity to act, with no office at all.
branches.cn: 能力线：抽象义指行动的能力，与任何机构无关。

branches.en: THE CHANNEL: when help passes through an agent, that link becomes a means.
branches.cn: 渠道线：帮助经由代理人传递时，这层连接本身成了手段。

branches.en: THE NEWS: one organization acts for many outlets at once.
branches.cn: 新闻线：一个机构同时替多家媒体办事。

intro.en: Agency is a Latin participle stem plus a Latin noun suffix, later reshaped by English endings.
intro.cn: agency 由拉丁分词词干加拉丁名词后缀构成，后来又经英语后缀改造。

latinIntro.en: Agere and agentia are recorded Latin words; no reconstructed root is needed for this family.
latinIntro.cn: agere 与 agentia 都是有记录的拉丁词，这个词族无需依赖重构形式。

items.example: Agere is the verb behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: agere 是整个词族背后的动词。

items.example: The stem names the doer of an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干指行动的执行者。

items.example: It forms agentia.
It forms agency from agent.
items.exampleCN: 它把 agent 变成 agency。

items.example: It forms agential.
It forms interagency.
It forms subagency.
They announced an agency-wide review.
items.exampleCN: 他们宣布了一次全机构范围的审查。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「代理的；能动性的」
由前缀加本词构成，义为「跨机构的」
由前缀加本词构成，义为「分代理处」

definition_zh: 议程；议事日程；待办事项；政策议题；隐秘意图
definition_en: a list of things to be discussed or done, or the set of issues a group intends to pursue
core_image: 一张纸，上面一行行写着待办的事，像队列一样往前排
scene: 会议开始前，秘书把要讨论的条目一条条写进本子。The chair read the agenda aloud before the discussion began.
sceneCN: 这里 agenda 是「会议议程」（第 1 个义项：会上要逐条讨论的清单）；句意为主席在讨论开始前把议程念了一遍。

pos.zh: 名词：议程；待办事项；政策议题

collocations.zh: 隐秘议程；未明说的意图

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁单数形式回构而来，义为「待办事项；议程中的一项」
由本词加动名词构成的复合词，义为「议题设置」

senses.title: A list of items for a meeting
senses.definition: a list of the matters to be discussed at a meeting, usually in order
senses.definitionCN: 会上要讨论的事项清单，通常按顺序排列
senses.example: The chair read the agenda aloud before the discussion began.
senses.exampleCN: 主席在讨论开始前把议程念了一遍。
senses.why: Latin agenda literally means things to be done, and a meeting list is the most direct modern use.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 agenda 字面就是「要做的事」，会议清单是最直接的现代用法。

senses.title: A list of things to be done
senses.definition: a set of tasks that someone plans to deal with
senses.definitionCN: 某人打算逐项处理的一组任务
senses.example: My agenda for the weekend is short: rest and repair the bike.
senses.exampleCN: 我周末的待办事项很短：休息，修自行车。
senses.why: Strip away the meeting and only the schedule of work remains, which is the word at its plainest.
senses.whyCN: 把会议这个场景去掉，剩下的就是一份工作清单，这是这个词最朴素的意思。

senses.title: The issues a group intends to pursue
senses.definition: the set of problems or goals that a government, party, or organization intends to act on
senses.definitionCN: 政府、政党或组织打算着手处理的问题或目标
senses.example: Climate change is high on the political agenda.
senses.exampleCN: 气候变化在政治议程上位置很高。
senses.why: A list of things to do, scaled up to a whole institution, becomes the programme it intends to carry out.
senses.whyCN: 一份待办清单放大到整个机构，就成了它打算推行的纲领。

senses.title: An unstated real purpose
senses.titleCN: 隐秘议程；未明说的意图
senses.definition: the real motive behind someone's actions, which they do not admit publicly
senses.definitionCN: 某人行动背后真实却不公开承认的动机
senses.example: The quiet donation hid a hidden agenda of tax relief.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔低调的捐赠背后藏着减税的隐秘意图。
senses.why: If the public list can be written, a private list can also exist, and hidden agenda names it.
senses.whyCN: 既然公开的清单可以写出来，私下的清单也可能存在，hidden agenda 指的就是后者。

intro.en: Agenda is a Latin word taken whole into English, not a word built inside English.
intro.cn: agenda 是整个从拉丁语搬进英语的，并不是在英语内部构造出来的词。

items.en: Agere meant to do or to drive, and it supplies the root of the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 agere 意为「做、驱动」，提供整个词族的词根。

items.en: Agenda is the neuter plural of the gerundive, meaning the things that are to be done.
items.cn: agenda 是动形词的中性复数，意为「那些应当被做的事」。

items.en: The singular agendum means one thing to be done; English later borrowed it back as a countable noun.
items.cn: 单数 agendum 指一件待办之事；英语后来又把这一个词借回来作可数名词。

items.en: The plural was borrowed as a singular English noun in the seventeenth century. First recorded dates vary and are not fully certain.
items.cn: 这个复数形式在十七世纪被借作英语单数名词。各家记录的首见年代略有出入，不能完全确定。

items.en: The political sense of a programme of issues became dominant in the twentieth century, and hidden agenda followed in journalism.
items.cn: 指一整套政策议题的政治义在二十世纪成为主流，新闻语言里随后又出现 hidden agenda。

note.en: The look-alike group is the agere family, where the same verb yields the doer, the office and the list; the near-meaning group is other words for ordered lists and plans.
note.cn: 形近组是 agere 词族，同一动词生出做事的人、办事的机构与待办的清单；近义组是其他表示有序清单与计划的词。

entries.definition: The person who acts, from the participle of the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代理人」，来自同一动词的分词形式。

entries.definition: The office or power of acting, from the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代理机构、能动性」，同出这一动词。

entries.definition: The singular form of agenda, meaning one item to be done.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一项待办事项」，是 agenda 的单数形式。

entries.definition: A plan that lists times and tasks, with the stress on when things happen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「日程表」，强调各项事情发生的时间。

entries.definition: A table of times for classes, trains, or events.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「时间表」，多用于课程、列车或活动的时间安排。

entries.definition: A planned series of actions or events; broader than agenda and less itemised.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「计划、方案」，比 agenda 宽泛，条目也更粗略。

entries.definition: A detailed plan of a journey, listing places and times.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行程表」，专指旅行路线与时间安排。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the literal Latin meaning and the phrases agenda appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用拉丁语的字面义，以及 agenda 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Agenda literally means things to be done, which is why a meeting has one.
normal.cn: agenda 字面意为「要做的事」，所以会议总要有一份议程。

normal.en: Agent and agenda share a root: the one who does, and the things to do.
normal.cn: agent 与 agenda 同根：一个指做事的人，一个指要做的事。

normal.en: On the agenda means waiting to be discussed, not yet settled.
normal.cn: on the agenda 指等待讨论，尚未定论。

normal.en: Set the agenda means deciding what others will talk about.
normal.cn: set the agenda 意为决定别人要谈什么。

normal.en: A hidden agenda is a private list that never gets printed.
normal.cn: hidden agenda 是一份从不印出来的私人清单。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of paper with ruled lines; each line is one task waiting its turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一张划了横线的纸，每一行都是一项等着轮到自己的任务。

abstract.en: Change the size of the paper and it becomes an institution's programme of issues.
abstract.cn: 把这张纸放大，它就变成一个机构的一整套政策议题。

abstract.en: Fold the paper and keep it in a pocket: that is the hidden agenda no one else reads.
abstract.cn: 把纸折起来塞进口袋：这就是别人读不到的隐秘议程。

examples.en: The chair read the agenda aloud before the discussion began.
examples.cn: 主席在讨论开始前把议程念了一遍。

examples.en: Climate change is high on the political agenda.
examples.cn: 气候变化在政治议程上位置很高。

examples.en: They set the agenda for the whole debate.
examples.cn: 他们为整场辩论设定了议题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额，干点啥」——把要做的事一条条列清：议程

root: 拉丁语 agenda 是动词 agere「做」的动形词中性复数，字面义「应当被做的事」；十七世纪整词借入英语，二十世纪扩展为「政策议题」，新闻用语中又衍生出 hidden agenda。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from a printed meeting list to any list of tasks, then to a whole institution's programme of issues, and finally to the private list someone hides.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从一张印好的会议清单，扩展到任何任务清单，再到整个机构的议题纲领，最后到某人藏起来的私人清单。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruled sheet of paper on which tasks are written one per line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张划了横线的纸，每行写一项任务。

branches.en: THE MEETING: the list is read aloud so that discussion follows a fixed order.
branches.cn: 会议线：清单被当众念出，讨论按固定次序进行。

branches.en: THE TASKS: without a meeting, the same list is simply the work waiting to be done.
branches.cn: 任务线：离开会议场景，同一份清单就是等着被做的工作。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: the list grows into the programme a government or party intends to carry out.
branches.cn: 机构线：清单放大成政府或政党打算推行的纲领。

branches.en: THE PRIVATE LIST: a motive can also be listed, but kept out of sight.
branches.cn: 私单线：动机同样可以列成清单，只是不给人看。

branches.en: THE ORDER: both the meeting list and the task list share one shape, items in sequence.
branches.cn: 次序线：会议清单与任务清单形状相同，都是按顺序排列的条目。

intro.en: Agenda is a Latin inflection rather than a derived English word; its parts are the verb root and the gerundive ending.
intro.cn: agenda 是一个拉丁语屈折形式，而不是英语派生词；它的成分是动词词根与动形词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Agere, agenda and agendum are all recorded forms, so nothing here is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: agere、agenda 与 agendum 都是有记录的形式，此处没有重构成分。

items.example: The verb root is shared with agent and agency.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根与 agent、agency 共用。

items.example: The form was borrowed whole into English.
items.exampleCN: 这个形式被整词借入英语。

items.example: English later revived it as a countable noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语后来把它复活为可数名词。

items.example: It marks obligation in the Latin form.
items.exampleCN: 它在拉丁形式中标记「应当」。

items.example: It makes the singular into a list.
items.exampleCN: 它把单数变成一份清单。

items.example: It forms agenda-setting.

items.structure: English noun from the same root
items.example: Agent and agenda are siblings, not parent and child.
items.exampleCN: agent 与 agenda 是同族兄弟，不是父子关系。

items.structure: English noun from the same root
items.example: Agency belongs to the same Latin family.
items.exampleCN: agency 属于同一拉丁词族。

由本词加动名词构成的复合词，义为「议题设置」

definition_zh: 代理人；经纪人；特工；作用剂；施事者；智能体
definition_en: a person or thing that acts, especially one who acts for another person or organization
core_image: 一个替别人出面的人，胸前别着别人的名签
scene: 警局走廊尽头站着一个陌生人，只说自己是为公家办事的。A government agent met the witness in a quiet café near the station.
sceneCN: 这里 agent 是「特工、公务人员」（第 2 个义项：为政府或机构秘密或正式办事的人）；句意为一名政府特工在车站附近的安静咖啡馆见了证人。

pos.zh: 名词：代理人；特工；作用剂；施事者

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁词干加名词后缀构成，义为「代理机构；能动性」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「代理人的；能动性的」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「施事的；执行动作的」
由前缀 sub- 加本词构成，义为「副代理人；子代理」

senses.title: Someone who acts for another
senses.definition: a person who is paid to act for another person or company, especially in business
senses.definitionCN: 受雇替他人或公司出面办事的人，尤指商务场合
senses.example: Her agent negotiated the book deal for her.
senses.exampleCN: 她的经纪人替她谈成了这本书的合约。
senses.why: The Latin participle names the one who acts, and acting for a client is its oldest everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词本指「行动者」，而替客户出面办事是它最早的日常用法。

senses.title: A secret or official operative
senses.definition: a person who works secretly for a government or an organization
senses.definitionCN: 为政府或组织秘密工作的人
senses.example: A government agent met the witness in a quiet café near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 一名政府特工在车站附近的安静咖啡馆见了证人。
senses.why: An operative also acts for an employer, only the acting is hidden.
senses.whyCN: 特工同样替雇主行动，只是这种行动是隐蔽的。

senses.title: A substance that produces an effect
senses.definition: a chemical or natural substance that causes a particular effect
senses.definitionCN: 能引起某种特定作用的化学或天然物质
senses.example: Bleach is a strong cleaning agent.
senses.exampleCN: 漂白剂是一种强效清洁剂。
senses.why: Once anything can act, the word extends from people to substances that act on other things.
senses.whyCN: 既然任何东西都能「起作用」，这个词就从人扩展到对其他物质起作用的物质。

senses.title: A person or force that causes change
senses.definition: a person, group, or force that causes a change in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 引起局面改变的人、群体或力量
senses.example: She was the agent of change in a very traditional office.
senses.exampleCN: 在一间非常传统的办公室里，她是推动改变的人。
senses.why: The participle keeps its active force: whatever brings a change about is doing something.
senses.whyCN: 分词保留了主动的意味：凡是带来改变的，都在「做」某件事。

senses.title: A piece of software acting on request
senses.definition: a program that performs tasks automatically on behalf of a user or another program
senses.definitionCN: 代表用户或另一程序自动执行任务的程序
senses.example: The mail agent filtered the spam before it reached her inbox.
senses.exampleCN: 邮件代理在垃圾邮件进入她的收件箱前就把它筛掉了。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the human role: software that acts in your place is literally your agent.
senses.whyCN: 计算领域借用了人的角色：代替你行动的软件，字面上就是你的代理人。

senses.title: The doer of an action in grammar
senses.definition: the person or thing that carries out the action of a verb, especially in a passive sentence
senses.definitionCN: 执行动词动作的人或物，尤指被动句中的施动者
senses.example: In the passive sentence, the agent appears after by.
senses.exampleCN: 在被动句里，施事出现在 by 之后。
senses.why: Grammar needed a precise name for the doer, and reused the general word for one who acts.
senses.whyCN: 语法需要给动作执行者一个精确的名称，于是复用了这个泛指行动者的词。

intro.en: Agent is the Latin participle of agere, borrowed straight into English and then extended to spies, chemicals and software.
intro.cn: agent 是拉丁语 agere 的分词形式，直接被英语借入，再扩展到特工、药剂与软件。

items.en: Agere meant to do, drive, or act, and it is the verb behind agent, agenda and agency.
items.cn: 拉丁语 agere 意为「做、驱动、行动」，是 agent、agenda 与 agency 共同的动词来源。

items.en: The present participle agens, stem agent-, meant acting or the one who acts.
items.cn: 现在分词 agens（词干 agent-）意为「正在行动的」或「行动者」。

items.en: In medieval usage an agent was a deputy or one entrusted with another's business.
items.cn: 在中世纪用法中，agent 指代理人或受托办理他人事务者。

items.en: The word enters English as the name of one who acts or has power to act. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词进入英语时指行动者或有行动权的人。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The spy sense, the chemical sense and the computing sense were all added later, each extending the idea of acting on someone's behalf.
items.cn: 特工义、化学药剂义与计算机义都是后来增加的，每一次都在延伸「替人起作用」这一观念。

note.en: The look-alike group is the agere family; the near-meaning group gathers people and roles that stand in for someone else.
note.cn: 形近组是 agere 词族；近义组收替他人出面的各种人与角色。

entries.definition: The office or capacity of acting, built on the same participle stem.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代理机构、能动性」，建立在同一分词词干上。

entries.definition: The list of things to be done, from the gerundive of the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「议程」，来自同一动词的动形词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning belonging to an agent or to agency.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「代理人的、能动性的」，由本词加后缀构成。

entries.definition: An adjective used in grammar for a form that marks the doer.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，语法术语，指标记施事的形式。

entries.definition: Someone chosen to speak or act for a group, often with official status.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代表」，指被选出来替群体发言或行事的人，常具正式身份。

entries.definition: A person who arranges deals between buyers and sellers for a fee.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「经纪人」，指收取费用在买卖双方之间撮合交易的人。

entries.definition: A go-between who carries messages or deals between two sides.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「中间人、调解者」，指在双方之间传递消息或促成交易的人。

entries.definition: Someone who secretly collects information, usually for a government.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「间谍」，指秘密搜集情报的人，多为政府服务。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the participle meaning and the phrases agent appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用分词含义，以及 agent 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Agens means acting, so an agent is simply the one who acts.
normal.cn: agens 意为「正在行动的」，所以 agent 就是那个行动的人。

normal.en: Agent, agenda and agency are three children of the verb agere.
normal.cn: agent、agenda 与 agency 是动词 agere 的三个孩子。

normal.en: A travel agent acts for you when you cannot go to the counter yourself.
normal.cn: travel agent 在你没法亲自去柜台时替你办事。

normal.en: A cleaning agent is a substance that acts on dirt.
normal.cn: cleaning agent 是对污垢起作用的物质。

normal.en: An agent of change is anyone or anything that makes a situation move.
normal.cn: agent of change 指任何让局面发生变动的人或物。

abstract.en: Picture a person wearing another person's name badge at a meeting: that is an agent at work.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人开会时别着别人的名牌：这就是代理人在办事。

abstract.en: The badge can be pinned to a spy, a bottle of cleaner, or a piece of software.
abstract.cn: 这枚名牌可以别在特工身上，也可以贴在一瓶清洁剂或一段软件上。

abstract.en: In every case someone or something acts, and someone else is spared the acting.
abstract.cn: 无论哪种情形，都是某人或某物在行动，而另一个人免于亲自行动。

examples.en: Her agent negotiated the book deal for her.
examples.cn: 她的经纪人替她谈成了这本书的合约。

examples.en: A government agent met the witness in a quiet café near the station.
examples.cn: 一名政府特工在车站附近的安静咖啡馆见了证人。

examples.en: She was the agent of change in a very traditional office.
examples.cn: 在一间非常传统的办公室里，她是推动改变的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶，真替」——真替别人出面办事：代理人

root: 拉丁语 agere「做、行动」的现在分词 agens（词干 agent-）意为「行动者」，中世纪指受托代办他人事务的人；英语借入后相继扩展出特工、化学药剂、软件代理与语法施事等义。

sensesIntro.en: All six senses name something that acts: a business stand-in, a hidden operative, a chemical that acts on matter, a force that drives change, software acting for a user, and the doer in a sentence.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都指「起作用者」：商务代办、隐蔽特工、对物质起作用的药剂、推动改变的力量、替用户行动的软件，以及句子里动作的执行者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person wears someone else's name badge and acts in that person's place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人别着别人的名牌，替那个人出面行动。

branches.en: THE CLIENT: the agent speaks and signs where the client cannot or will not.
branches.cn: 委托人线：代理人替委托人出面说话与签字。

branches.en: THE SHADOW: the same acting is done secretly for a state or an organization.
branches.cn: 暗线：同样的代行由国家或组织秘密安排。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: the word leaves people behind and names chemicals that act on matter.
branches.cn: 物质线：这个词离开人，转指对物质起作用的化学品。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: anything that makes a situation change is acting, so it is an agent.
branches.cn: 动因线：凡使局面改变者都在「行动」，因此都是 agent。

branches.en: THE STAND-IN: software and the grammar term both borrow the human role of the doer.
branches.cn: 代行线：软件与语法术语都借用了「行动者」这一人的角色。

intro.en: Agent is a Latin participle plus an English noun use; English then adds ordinary suffixes around it.
intro.cn: agent 是拉丁分词被英语当作名词使用，英语随后又在它周围加了普通后缀。

latinIntro.en: Agere and its participle are recorded Latin forms, so only the deeper root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: agere 及其分词都是有记录的拉丁形式，只有更早的词根属于重构。

items.example: Agere is the shared root of the family.
items.exampleCN: agere 是这个词族共用的词根。

items.example: Agens is the direct source of agent.
items.exampleCN: agens 是 agent 的直接来源。

items.example: It marks the doer in the Latin form.
items.exampleCN: 它在拉丁形式中标记行动者。

items.example: It forms agency.
It forms agential.
It forms agentive.
It forms subagent.

items.meaning: someone free to act or choose
items.meaningCN: 可自由行动或选择的人
items.example: After the contract ended, he was a free agent.
items.exampleCN: 合同结束后，他成了自由身。

definition_zh: 侵略；侵犯；攻击行为；好斗性
definition_en: an attack or hostile act against another person or country, or the readiness to attack
core_image: 一步跨到别人面前，抬手把对方的地界推开
scene: 球场上双方推搡起来，裁判跑进场内把人群分开。The referee stopped the match after a clear act of aggression by the visiting team.
sceneCN: 这里 aggression 是「攻击行为、侵犯」（第 2 个义项：对他人施加的物理攻击）；句意为客队出现明显的侵犯动作后，裁判中止了比赛。

pos.zh: 名词：侵略；攻击行为；好斗性

derivatives.zh: 由本词加施事后缀 -or 构成，义为「侵略者；攻击者」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「侵略的；好斗的」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「好斗性；攻击性」
由本词回构出的动词，义为「侵犯；挑衅」

senses.title: An attack on a country
senses.definition: the act of attacking another country or territory without just cause
senses.definitionCN: 无正当理由攻击他国或他国领土的行为
senses.example: The court condemned the military aggression against the neighbouring state.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭谴责了对邻国的军事侵略。
senses.why: Latin aggredi meant to step towards something, and stepping towards a border with force became invasion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aggredi 意为「迈向某物」，带着武力迈向边界，就成了侵略。

senses.title: A physical attack
senses.definition: a physical act of attacking a person or an animal
senses.definitionCN: 对人或者动物施加的物理攻击行为
senses.example: The referee stopped the match after a clear act of aggression by the visiting team.
senses.exampleCN: 客队出现明显的侵犯动作后，裁判中止了比赛。
senses.why: The same stepping-forward motion, applied to one person instead of a state, is a blow or a shove.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「向前迈一步」的动作，用在一个人而非一个国家身上，就是一拳或一推。

senses.title: Hostile feelings and behaviour
senses.definition: the tendency to behave in a hostile or attacking way, even without a blow
senses.definitionCN: 以敌对或攻击方式行事的倾向，即使没有动手
senses.example: Verbal aggression can do as much harm as a blow.
senses.exampleCN: 言语攻击造成的伤害不亚于一记拳头。
senses.why: If attack can be physical, it can also be a habit of mind that shows in words and tone.
senses.whyCN: 既然攻击可以是身体动作，它也可以是一种表现在言辞和语气里的心理习惯。

senses.title: A studied behaviour pattern
senses.definition: the behaviour studied in psychology and ethology as intentional harm-doing
senses.definitionCN: 心理学与动物行为学研究的、带有意伤害的行为模式
senses.example: Researchers study aggression in young children and in territorial animals.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者考察幼儿与护领地动物的攻击性。
senses.why: Science needed a neutral label for harm-doing, and took the everyday word for attack.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要一个中性标签来指「施加伤害」，于是取用了日常表示攻击的词。

intro.en: Aggression is built on a Latin verb for stepping forward, and the stepping turned into an attack.
intro.cn: aggression 建立在一个表示「向前迈步」的拉丁动词上，这一步迈出去就变成了攻击。

items.en: Gradi meant to step or walk, and it is the root shared with congress and progress.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gradi 意为「迈步、行走」，与 congress、progress 共享这个词根。

items.en: Ad plus gradi formed aggredi, to approach someone, and from there to attack them.
items.cn: ad 加 gradi 构成 aggredi，意为「走近某人」，并由此引申为「攻击」。

items.en: The noun aggressio named an attack or an onset, especially in military writing.
items.cn: 名词 aggressio 指攻击或突袭，多用于军事文本。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the seventeenth century, first in the sense of an unprovoked attack. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个名词，最早指无端发动的攻击。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Psychology gave the word its modern technical sense of harm-doing behaviour in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 心理学在二十世纪赋予这个词现代的专业义，指施加伤害的行为模式。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin stepping root and shows how different prefixes redirect it; the near-meaning group gathers kinds of attack and hostility.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁「迈步」词根，并显示不同前缀如何改变方向；近义组收各类攻击与敌意。

entries.definition: The one who attacks first, formed from the same Latin noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「侵略者」，由同一拉丁名词构成。

entries.definition: The adjective for someone or something ready to attack.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「侵略的、好斗的」，同出这一词根。

entries.definition: A formal meeting where people come together; con- means together, so the root gradi gives a coming together rather than a stepping at someone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「代表大会」；前缀 con- 表示「共同」，同一 gradi 词根在这里是「走到一起」，不是逼近他人。

entries.definition: The act of going out; it merely looks like aggression and comes from e- plus gradi in the sense of stepping out.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「外出、退出」；只是与 aggression 拼写相近，其构成是 e- 加 gradi「走出」，语义方向完全不同。

entries.definition: The entry of an army into another country by force, wider in scale than a single act.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「入侵」，指军队以武力进入他国，规模比单次侵犯更大。

entries.definition: A direct act of violence against a person or place; the plainest word of the group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「攻击」，最朴素直接的用词。

entries.definition: Unfriendly feeling or opposition, which may exist without any physical act.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「敌意、敌对状态」，可以只存在于情绪与态度中。

entries.definition: A violent physical attack, and in law a specific offence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「袭击、殴打」，在法律语境中是具体罪名。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin stepping root and the phrases aggression appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用拉丁「迈步」词根，以及 aggression 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Gradi means to step, so aggression is a step taken towards someone with force.
normal.cn: gradi 意为「迈步」，所以 aggression 是带着武力朝别人迈出的那一步。

normal.en: Congress uses the same root with con-, where people step together instead of at each other.
normal.cn: congress 用同一词根加 con-，那里的人是走到一起，而不是逼近对方。

normal.en: Acts of aggression is the standard phrase in law and diplomacy.
normal.cn: acts of aggression 是法律与外交文本中的标准说法。

normal.en: Verbal aggression is attack without a blow.
normal.cn: verbal aggression 是没有动手的攻击。

normal.en: Passive aggression hides hostility inside silence or delay.
normal.cn: passive aggression 把敌意藏进沉默或拖延里。

abstract.en: Picture a foot lifted and moving across a boundary line: the moment it lands, a step becomes an invasion.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚抬起，越过一条边界线：落地那一刻，迈步就成了侵略。

abstract.en: The same foot can step towards a person, a country, or a conversation.
abstract.cn: 同一只脚可以迈向一个人、一个国家，也可以迈向一场对话。

abstract.en: If the foot never lands but stays raised, the hostility is still there, only unspoken.
abstract.cn: 如果那只脚始终不落地、只是悬着，敌意依然存在，只是没有说出口。

examples.en: The court condemned the military aggression against the neighbouring state.
examples.cn: 法庭谴责了对邻国的军事侵略。

examples.en: Verbal aggression can do as much harm as a blow.
examples.cn: 言语攻击造成的伤害不亚于一记拳头。

examples.en: Researchers study aggression in young children and in territorial animals.
examples.cn: 研究者考察幼儿与护领地动物的攻击性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额，哥来神」——哥哥猛冲上前：侵略、攻击

root: 拉丁语 gradi「迈步、行走」加前缀 ad-「向」构成 aggredi「走近」，再引申为「攻击」，名词 aggressio 指突袭；英语十七世纪借入为「无端攻击」，二十世纪由心理学扩展为「攻击性行为模式」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses follow one movement: a step taken towards another. At the scale of states it is invasion, at the scale of bodies it is a blow, at the scale of temper it is hostility, and in science it is a named behaviour pattern.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项跟随同一个动作：朝他人迈出的一步。放大到国家就是侵略，缩小到身体就是动手，落在脾气上就是敌意，进入科学就成为被命名的行为模式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot crosses a boundary line and lands inside someone else's space.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚越过边界线，落在别人的地界里。

branches.en: THE STATE: the foot belongs to an army and the boundary is a national border.
branches.cn: 国家线：这只脚属于军队，边界是国界。

branches.en: THE BODY: the same step lands on one person as a blow or a shove.
branches.cn: 身体线：同一步落在一个具体的人身上，成为一拳或一推。

branches.en: THE TEMPER: the step is never taken, but the readiness to take it remains.
branches.cn: 情绪线：这一步始终没有迈出，但迈出的准备状态一直存在。

branches.en: THE LABEL: science names the whole pattern of intentional harm-doing.
branches.cn: 学术线：科学为有意施加伤害的整套模式命名。

branches.en: THE SCALE: one motion serves both a nation and a single body, only the size changes.
branches.cn: 尺度线：同一个动作既用于国家也用于个人，变的只是尺度。

intro.en: Aggression joins a Latin prefix, a Latin verb root and a Latin noun ending, and English adds the rest of the family with its own suffixes.
intro.cn: aggression 由拉丁前缀、拉丁动词词根与拉丁名词词尾构成，词族其余成员由英语后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: Gradi, aggredi and aggressio are recorded Latin forms; the family needs no reconstructed root.
latinIntro.cn: gradi、aggredi 与 aggressio 都是有记录的拉丁形式，这个词族无需重构词根。

items.exampleCN: 它把「迈步」的方向指向某人。

items.exampleCN: gradi 与 congress、progress 共享词根。

items.example: The prefix turns walking into approaching.
The noun came into English almost unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词几乎原样进入英语。

items.example: It marks the noun of action.
It forms aggressor.
It forms aggressive.
It forms aggressiveness.

由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「侵略的」

definition_zh: 侵略的；好斗的；有进取心的；强硬的；猛烈的
definition_en: ready to attack or to act with force, and by extension very determined or intense
core_image: 身子前倾、肩膀抬起，随时准备冲出去
scene: 门铃一响，院子里的狗立刻竖起背毛，挡在门口。The dog became aggressive whenever strangers approached the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 aggressive 是「好斗的、有攻击性的」（第 2 个义项：遇人就想扑咬的性情）；句意为只要有人靠近大门，那条狗就变得凶猛好斗。

pos.zh: 形容词：侵略的；好斗的；有进取心的；强硬的

collocations.zh: 攻击性行为；好斗的表现

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉后缀加名词词尾构成，义为「侵略；攻击行为」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「咄咄逼人地；强劲地」

senses.title: Ready to attack
senses.definition: willing or likely to attack another person, group, or country
senses.definitionCN: 愿意或很可能攻击他人、他国或他群体的
senses.example: The report described an aggressive policy towards smaller neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把针对较小邻国的政策描述为侵略性的。
senses.why: The adjective simply turns aggression into a quality someone carries before any act happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把 aggression 变成一种在行动之前就带着的性情。

senses.title: Hostile in manner
senses.definition: behaving in a threatening or hostile way towards other people or animals
senses.definitionCN: 对人或者动物表现出威胁、敌意的
senses.example: The dog became aggressive whenever strangers approached the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 只要有人靠近大门，那条狗就变得凶猛好斗。
senses.why: An animal that steps towards a stranger is showing the same forward motion as an army at a border.
senses.whyCN: 朝陌生人逼近的动物，表现出的正是军队逼近边界时那种向前的动作。

senses.title: Very determined in pursuing goals
senses.definition: very determined and energetic in trying to succeed, sometimes admired and sometimes resented
senses.definitionCN: 为求成功而极其坚决、用力，有时受人赞赏，有时招人反感
senses.example: She was an aggressive young lawyer who never lost a case she wanted.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个进取心很强的年轻律师，想赢的案子从不失手。
senses.why: In business the attack loses its violence and keeps only its force, so it becomes a virtue.
senses.whyCN: 在商业语境里，攻击性去掉了暴力成分，只留下那股劲，于是成了褒义。

senses.title: Forceful or pushy in method
senses.definition: using forceful, persistent methods that may make others uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 采用强硬、紧逼的手段，可能让别人不舒服
senses.example: Their aggressive sales calls annoyed most of the residents.
senses.exampleCN: 他们咄咄逼人的推销电话让大多数居民反感。
senses.why: Pushiness is attack moved into conversation, where pressure replaces the blow.
senses.whyCN: 咄咄逼人就是把攻击搬进交谈，用压力代替拳头。

senses.title: Intense in strength or extent
senses.definition: very strong, fast, or thorough, especially of a disease or a medical treatment
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病或治疗非常强烈、迅速或彻底
senses.example: Doctors chose a more aggressive treatment for the fast-growing tumour.
senses.exampleCN: 医生为这个生长迅速的肿瘤选择了更激进的治疗方案。
senses.why: If the core idea is force applied without hesitation, medicine can use it for treatments that hold nothing back.
senses.whyCN: 如果核心观念是毫不犹豫地用尽全力，医学就可以用它形容不留余地的治疗。

intro.en: Aggressive is the adjective built on the Latin noun for an attack; its later senses soften or redirect that force.
intro.cn: aggressive 是建立在拉丁语「攻击」名词上的形容词；它后来的义项把这份力软化或改向。

items.en: The root means to step or walk, and with ad- it gives aggredi, to approach and attack.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「迈步、行走」，加 ad- 构成 aggredi，意为「走近并攻击」。

items.en: The noun aggressio named an attack, and English took it as aggression.
items.cn: 名词 aggressio 指攻击，英语借入为 aggression。

items.en: The suffix -ivus formed adjectives meaning tending to do something, which became English -ive.
items.cn: 后缀 -ivus 构成表示「倾向于做某事」的形容词，在英语中变为 -ive。

items.en: The adjective appears in English in the eighteenth century, first in the military sense of attacking. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十八世纪见于英语，最早用于军事上的「进攻的」。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The business sense of energetic and the medical sense of intense both date from later usage, each keeping the idea of force.
items.cn: 商业上的「进取」义与医学上的「强力」义都属后来的用法，两者都保留了「用力」这一观念。

note.en: The look-alike group is the aggression family; the near-meaning group gathers words for forcefulness, some positive and some hostile.
note.cn: 形近组是 aggression 词族；近义组收表示「强势用力」的词，其中有褒有贬。

entries.definition: The noun for an attack or for hostile behaviour in general.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「侵略、攻击行为」，是同族的基础名词。

entries.definition: The person or country that attacks first.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「侵略者」，指先行攻击的一方。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a forceful or hostile manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「咄咄逼人地、强劲地」，由本词加后缀构成。

entries.definition: Confident in stating one's own needs without attacking others; usually approving.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「坚定自信的」，指清楚表达自身需求而不攻击他人，通常含褒义。

entries.definition: Strong and clear in action or speech, without the hostility of aggressive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「强有力的、明确的」，不带 aggressive 那种敌意。

entries.definition: Openly unfriendly or opposed; it stresses attitude rather than forward motion.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「敌对的」，强调态度而非向前的动作。

entries.definition: Eager to argue or fight, with a strongly competitive edge.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「好斗的、爱争辩的」，带强烈竞争意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin attack root and the phrases aggressive appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用拉丁「攻击」词根，以及 aggressive 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Aggression is the noun and aggressive is the adjective: the same force, now a quality.
normal.cn: aggression 是名词，aggressive 是形容词：同一股力，变成了性情。

normal.en: Aggressive behaviour is the standard phrase in psychology for harmful acting out.
normal.cn: aggressive behaviour 是心理学里指有害行为的标准说法。

normal.en: Aggressive marketing pushes a product at customers rather than waiting.
normal.cn: aggressive marketing 指主动把产品推向顾客，而不是等着顾客上门。

normal.en: An aggressive treatment holds nothing back, even if it is hard on the patient.
normal.cn: aggressive treatment 指不留余地的治疗，即使对病人负担很重。

normal.en: Assertive is the approving cousin of aggressive: firm without the attack.
normal.cn: assertive 是 aggressive 的褒义近亲：坚定而不带攻击。

abstract.en: Picture a body leaning forward with shoulders raised: the posture arrives before the action.
abstract.cn: 想象一个身体前倾、肩膀抬起的姿态：动作还没发生，姿态先到了。

abstract.en: Move that posture into a sales call and it becomes pressure instead of a blow.
abstract.cn: 把这个姿态搬进推销电话，它就变成压力而不是拳头。

abstract.en: Move it into a hospital and it becomes a treatment that refuses to hold back.
abstract.cn: 把它搬进医院，它就成了一种不肯留余地的治疗。

examples.en: The dog became aggressive whenever strangers approached the gate.
examples.cn: 只要有人靠近大门，那条狗就变得凶猛好斗。

examples.en: Their aggressive sales calls annoyed most of the residents.
examples.cn: 他们咄咄逼人的推销电话让大多数居民反感。

examples.en: Doctors chose a more aggressive treatment for the fast-growing tumour.
examples.cn: 医生为这个生长迅速的肿瘤选择了更激进的治疗方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额，哥来媳妇」——哥哥护着家人往前冲：好斗的

root: 同族名词 aggression 出自拉丁语 aggressio「攻击」，其动词 aggredi 由 ad-「向」加 gradi「迈步」构成；加拉丁形容词后缀 -ivus（英语 -ive）成为 aggressive，本义「进攻的」，后扩展为「进取的、强硬的、猛烈的」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses keep one constant, force applied forward: against a country, against a person, towards a goal, into a conversation, and into a disease.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项保持同一个常量，即向前施加的力：对着国家、对着人、对着目标、伸进交谈，以及伸进疾病。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body leans forward with raised shoulders, ready to move first.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体前倾、肩膀抬起，准备先动。

branches.en: THE BORDER: the forward posture belongs to an army facing a weaker neighbour.
branches.cn: 国界线：这个前倾姿态属于面对弱邻的军队。

branches.en: THE BODY: the same posture in an animal shows as bared teeth and raised fur.
branches.cn: 身体线：同一姿态在动物身上表现为龇牙与竖毛。

branches.en: THE CAREER: the attack turns into drive, and the force is praised instead of feared.
branches.cn: 事业线：攻击转为干劲，这股力从被畏惧变成被赞赏。

branches.en: THE TALK: pressure replaces the blow, and the target is a customer or a listener.
branches.cn: 交谈线：压力取代拳头，承受者变成顾客或听众。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: the force is applied to a disease, with no hesitation left in it.
branches.cn: 诊疗线：这股力用在疾病上，其中不留任何迟疑。

intro.en: Aggressive is a Latin noun turned adjective by -ive, with English adverbs and nouns built on top.
intro.cn: aggressive 是拉丁名词经 -ive 变成形容词，英语再在其上构造副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Aggressio and the suffix -ivus are recorded, so no reconstructed root is used here.
latinIntro.cn: aggressio 与后缀 -ivus 都有记录，此处不使用重构词根。

items.example: It points the stepping at a target.
items.exampleCN: 它把「迈步」指向一个目标。

items.example: The root is shared with congress.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根与 congress 共用。

items.example: The verb supplies the meaning of attack.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「攻击」的含义。

items.example: It is the base of the whole family.
It turns the noun into aggressive.
It forms aggressively.
It forms aggressiveness.
It forms aggressor.

由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「咄咄逼人地」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「好斗性」

definition_zh: 以前；以往；之前
definition_en: before the present time, used after an expression of how long something has lasted
core_image: 脚印留在身后，离现在越走越远
scene: 桌上摊着一本旧相册，照片边角已经发白。Three years ago she moved to the coast and never came back.
sceneCN: 这里 ago 是「（距今）……以前」（第 2 个义项：与时间段连用，表示从现在往回数的时长）；句意为三年前她搬到海边，再没回来。

pos.zh: 副词：以前；以往

derivatives.zh: 由中古英语过去分词形式保留而来，义为「过去的；以前的」（古体）
中古英语的另一种拼写形式，义为「以前」（古体）

senses.title: Before the present
senses.definition: at a time in the past, seen as earlier than now
senses.definitionCN: 在过去某个时间，以现在为参照看作更早
senses.example: The letter arrived two days ago.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信两天前到了。
senses.why: The word began as a past participle meaning gone by, so anything ago has already passed the present.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是意为「已经过去」的过去分词，因此凡 ago 都在现在之前。

senses.title: With a length of time
senses.definition: used after a period of time to measure how far back an event lies
senses.definitionCN: 放在一段时间之后，用来量出某事距现在多远
senses.example: Three years ago she moved to the coast and never came back.
senses.exampleCN: 三年前她搬到海边，再没回来。
senses.why: A span of time plus ago turns the span into a measuring tape laid back from today.
senses.whyCN: 一段时间加 ago，等于把这段时间当成一条从今天往回铺的尺子。

senses.title: In the distant past
senses.definition: in a time so far back that it is treated as a separate age, as in long ago
senses.definitionCN: 在很久以前的时段，常视为另一个年代，如 long ago
senses.example: Long ago, this valley was covered by ice.
senses.exampleCN: 很久以前，这片山谷被冰雪覆盖。
senses.why: When the span is stretched to its limit, ago marks a past that is no longer connected to the present.
senses.whyCN: 当时间跨度拉到极限，ago 标记的是一个与现在不再相连的过去。

senses.title: Only a short time back
senses.definition: in the recent past, as in not long ago or a moment ago
senses.definitionCN: 在很近的过去，如 not long ago 或 a moment ago
senses.example: He called not long ago and left a short message.
senses.exampleCN: 他不久前打过电话，留了一句简短的话。
senses.why: The same measuring tape can be pulled back only a little, and then ago points at almost-now.
senses.whyCN: 同一条尺子只往回拉一点点，ago 就指向几乎等于现在的时刻。

intro.en: Ago began as a past participle of a verb meaning to go away, and the idea of having gone by became the idea of before now.
intro.cn: ago 最初是意为「离去」的动词的过去分词，「已经走过去」这一观念变成了「在现在之前」。

items.en: Gan meant to go, and it survives today only in the verb go.
items.cn: 古英语 gān 意为「走」，今天只保留在动词 go 里。

items.en: The prefixed form agan meant to go away or to pass by, with a- carrying the sense of away.
items.cn: 加前缀的形式 āgān 意为「走开、过去」，前缀 ā- 带「离开」之意。

items.en: The past participle agon meant gone by, and it was used after expressions of time.
items.cn: 过去分词 agon 意为「已经过去的」，用在表示时间的短语之后。

items.en: The form was shortened to ago and fixed in its modern position after the time phrase. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词形缩短为 ago，并固定在现代位置，即放在时间短语之后。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Long ago and not long ago became fixed phrases, using the same word to point at opposite ends of memory.
items.cn: long ago 与 not long ago 成为固定短语，同一个词分别指向记忆的两端。

note.en: The look-alike group has the archaic survivals of the same word plus one accidental resemblance; the near-meaning group is other adverbs for earlier time.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词的古老残留形式，另加一个偶然相似者；近义组收其他表示「更早」的副词。

entries.definition: An archaic adjective meaning gone by or past, kept from the fuller Middle English participle.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，古体，义为「过去的」；由中古英语较完整的分词形式保留而来。

entries.definition: An archaic spelling and form of ago found in older poetry.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，古体拼写，见于较早的诗歌，与 ago 同源。

entries.definition: The self or self-esteem; it merely looks similar and comes from Latin ego, meaning I.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自我、自尊心」；只是拼写相近，其词源是拉丁语代词 ego「我」。

entries.definition: Earlier than a given point in time; it can also be used of the future.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或介词，义为「在……之前」，也可用于未来。

entries.definition: At an earlier time, often stated in contrast with now; formal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「先前」，常与现在对照，语气正式。

entries.definition: At a time before the one being discussed, often within the same day or event.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「更早」，常指同一天或同一事件中更靠前的时刻。

entries.definition: In the past, used especially of names, roles, or states that have changed.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「从前」，多用于已经改变的名称、身份或状态。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real origin of the word and the time phrases it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这个词的真实来源，以及它出现的时间短语。

normal.en: Ago comes from a participle meaning gone by, so the past is literally behind us.
normal.cn: ago 来自意为「已经过去」的分词，所以过去确实在我们身后。

normal.en: The word always follows the time expression, never precedes it.
normal.cn: 这个词总是跟在时间短语之后，从不放在前面。

normal.en: Long ago and not long ago use the same word at opposite ends of the scale.
normal.cn: long ago 与 not long ago 用同一个词指向尺子的两端。

normal.en: Ago never takes an object: it looks back from now, not from another event.
normal.cn: ago 从不带宾语：它从现在往回看，而不是从另一件事往回看。

normal.en: The archaic agone is the fuller form that ago was cut down from.
normal.cn: 古体的 agone 就是 ago 被截短之前较完整的形式。

abstract.en: Picture footprints left on a path, each one further behind you than the last.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路上留下的脚印，每一个都比前一个更落在身后。

abstract.en: Lay a measuring tape from today backwards: the length you pull out is the time before ago starts.
abstract.cn: 从今天往回铺一条尺子：拉出的长度就是 ago 之前的那段时间。

abstract.en: Pull out a little and it is almost now; pull out a lot and the past becomes another age.
abstract.cn: 拉出一点点就几乎等于现在；拉出很长，过去就成了另一个年代。

examples.en: The letter arrived two days ago.
examples.cn: 这封信两天前到了。

examples.en: Long ago, this valley was covered by ice.
examples.cn: 很久以前，这片山谷被冰雪覆盖。

examples.en: He called not long ago and left a short message.
examples.cn: 他不久前打过电话，留了一句简短的话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额，够」——够了，都过去了：以前、之前

root: 古英语 gān「走」加前缀 ā-「离开」成为 āgān「走开、过去」，其过去分词 agon 意为「已经过去的」，十四世纪缩短为 ago，固定用在时间短语之后表示「距今……以前」。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses are one measuring trick: from now, look back a little, a lot, or by naming a length of time.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项是同一套度量办法：从现在往回看，看一点点、看很远，或者干脆报出一段时长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: footprints behind you on a path, each one further from where you stand.
core.cn: 核心意象：身后路上的脚印，每一个都离你站的地方更远。

branches.en: THE REFERENCE POINT: everything ago names lies on the far side of now.
branches.cn: 参照线：ago 指的一切都在现在的另一侧。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: a span of time becomes the tape that fixes how far back the event sits.
branches.cn: 度量线：一段时间成为尺子，量出事件落在多远的后方。

branches.en: THE FAR END: stretched to the limit, the past becomes an age of its own.
branches.cn: 远端线：拉到极限，过去就自成一个年代。

branches.en: THE NEAR END: pulled back only a little, the same word means almost now.
branches.cn: 近端线：只往回拉一点点，同一个词就指几乎等于现在。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: whether the span is named or implied, the word still points backwards from today.
branches.cn: 形状线：无论时长是说出的还是隐含的，这个词始终从今天往回指。

intro.en: Ago is not a derived word but a worn-down participle; its parts are the old prefix and the old verb for going.
intro.cn: ago 不是派生词，而是磨旧的过去分词；它的成分是古老的前缀与表示「走」的古动词。

latinIntro.en: This word is native English with no Latin relatives, so the Latin entries remain empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，没有拉丁同族词，因此拉丁条目留空。

items.example: It marks departure in the old verb agan.
items.exampleCN: 它在古动词 āgān 中标记「离去」。

items.example: Gan survives in modern go.
items.exampleCN: gān 在现代英语的 go 中留存。

items.example: The prefix and the verb together give the sense of passing.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与动词合起来给出「过去」的意思。

items.example: The participle is the direct source of ago.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词是 ago 的直接来源。

items.example: It marks the completed action in agon.
items.exampleCN: 它在 agon 中标记已完成的动作。

items.example: The fuller form survives in old poetry.
items.exampleCN: 较完整的形式保留在古诗中。

items.example: The variant appears in early verse.
items.exampleCN: 这个变体见于早期诗歌。

items.example: Long ago, the valley held a lake.
items.exampleCN: 很久以前，这片山谷里有一个湖。

definition_zh: 同意；赞成；商定；相符；适合
definition_en: to have the same opinion as someone, to say yes to something, or to be consistent with something
core_image: 两只手从两边伸过来，在同一处握在一起
scene: 会议室里两个人本来各说各的，争论了两个小时。After two hours of argument, both sides agreed on a new date for the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 agree 是「商定、达成一致」（第 3 个义项：就某事取得共同结论）；句意为争论两小时后，双方就新的会议日期达成了一致。

pos.zh: 动词：同意；赞成；商定；相符；适合

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「协议；一致」
由本词加后缀 -able 构成，义为「令人愉快的；可接受的」
由否定前缀 dis- 加本词构成，义为「不同意；不一致」
由否定前缀加本词再加后缀构成，义为「令人不快的」

senses.title: To have the same opinion
senses.definition: to share the same opinion as another person about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事与另一个人持相同看法
senses.example: I agree with you that the plan needs more time.
senses.exampleCN: 我同意你的看法，这个计划需要更多时间。
senses.why: Old French agreer first meant to be pleasing, and two opinions that please each other end up alike.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 agreer 最初意为「使愉快」，彼此合意的两种看法最终就变得相同。

senses.title: To say yes to something
senses.definition: to say that one is willing to do something or to accept an offer
senses.definitionCN: 表示愿意做某事，或接受某项提议
senses.example: She agreed to lead the project until spring.
senses.exampleCN: 她答应带这个项目到春天。
senses.why: Saying yes is the outward sign that the proposal suits you, and suit was the older meaning.
senses.whyCN: 说「好」是把「这件事合我意」表现出来，而「合意」正是这个词较早的意思。

senses.title: To reach a shared decision
senses.definition: to reach a decision together after discussion, especially about terms or plans
senses.definitionCN: 经讨论后共同作出决定，尤指关于条件或计划
senses.example: After two hours of argument, both sides agreed on a new date for the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 争论两小时后，双方就新的会议日期达成了一致。
senses.why: When two parties are pleased with the same terms, the terms become a settled agreement.
senses.whyCN: 当双方对同样的条件都满意时，这些条件就成了定下来的约定。

senses.title: To be consistent with something
senses.definition: to match or be consistent with another account, fact, or set of figures
senses.definitionCN: 与另一种说法、事实或数据相匹配、不矛盾
senses.example: His story does not agree with the times on the ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 他的说法与票上的时间对不上。
senses.why: Two records that suit each other are in harmony, so agree came to mean correspond.
senses.whyCN: 两份彼此合得上的记录就是和谐的，于是 agree 引申为「对得上」。

senses.title: To suit a person's body
senses.definition: to have a good or bad effect on someone, especially of food or climate
senses.definitionCN: 对某人身体产生好的或坏的影响，多指食物或气候
senses.example: Rich food does not agree with him in hot weather.
senses.exampleCN: 天热时油腻的食物他吃了不舒服。
senses.why: If something pleases the body, it agrees with it; the old sense of pleasing survives here intact.
senses.whyCN: 某物若让身体舒适，就是与身体「合得来」，这里保留了「使愉快」的古义。

senses.title: To match in grammar
senses.definition: to match another word in number, person, or gender, as subjects and verbs do
senses.definitionCN: 在数、人称或性上与另一个词相应，如主语与动词
senses.example: In this sentence the verb agrees with its subject in number.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个句子里，动词与主语在数上保持一致。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the general notion of harmony for forms that must correspond.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了「彼此和谐」的一般观念，用来指必须相互对应的形式。

intro.en: Agree goes back to a Latin adjective meaning pleasing, and pleasing turned into consenting and matching.
intro.cn: agree 可追溯到意为「令人愉快的」的拉丁形容词，而「合意」又演变为「同意」与「相符」。

items.en: Gratus meant pleasing, welcome, or thankful, and it is also the source of grateful and gratitude.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gratus 意为「令人愉快的、受欢迎的、感激的」，grateful 与 gratitude 也出自它。

items.en: The prefix ad- meant to or towards, and it combined with gratus in Vulgar Latin to express being pleasing to someone.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 意为「向、朝」，在俗拉丁语中与 gratus 结合，表示「对某人合意」。

items.en: Agreer meant to please, to be agreeable, and also to receive something kindly or consent to it.
items.cn: agreer 意为「使愉快、合意」，也指「乐于接受、同意」。

items.en: English agree first meant to please or to be pleasing, then to consent and to be in harmony. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 agree 最初意为「使愉快、合意」，随后指「同意」与「彼此和谐」。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The senses settled into consent, consistency, suitability, and grammatical correspondence, each keeping the idea of two things fitting together.
items.cn: 词义最后稳定为同意、相符、适合与语法对应，每个义项都保留「两物彼此相合」这一观念。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on agree and the Latin root gratus; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of consenting and corresponding.
note.cn: 形近组建立在 agree 与拉丁词根 gratus 上；近义组收表示「同意」与「相符」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for consent or for a formal arrangement between parties.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同意、协议」，由本词加后缀构成。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning pleasant or willing to accept something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人愉快的、愿意接受的」，由本词加后缀构成。

entries.definition: The opposite verb, built with the negative prefix dis-, meaning to hold a different opinion.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「不同意、不一致」，由否定前缀 dis- 加本词构成。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning thankful, from the same Latin adjective gratus.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「感激的」，与 agree 同出拉丁形容词 gratus。

entries.definition: To give permission or approval, often formally and often for something done by others.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「同意、准许」，常为正式许可，且多针对他人要做的事。

entries.definition: To share an opinion, used in formal writing and in official findings.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「意见相同」，用于正式文字与官方结论。

entries.definition: To agree to a proposal, especially after consideration; formal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「赞同、应允」，多指考虑之后同意提议，语气正式。

entries.definition: To match or be in line with something else, close to agree in its matching sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「相符、对应」，接近 agree 的「相符」义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the pleasing root and the preposition patterns that change the meaning of agree.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用「合意」词根，以及会改变 agree 含义的介词搭配。

normal.en: Gratus means pleasing, so to agree is for two minds to be pleased with the same thing.
normal.cn: gratus 意为「令人愉快的」，所以 agree 就是两颗心对同一件事都合意。

normal.en: Agree with a person, agree on a topic, agree to a proposal: the preposition decides the sense.
normal.cn: agree with 接人，agree on 接话题，agree to 接提议：介词决定意思。

normal.en: Grateful and agree share one Latin adjective, so thankfulness and consent are relatives.
normal.cn: grateful 与 agree 共用一个拉丁形容词，感激与同意本是亲戚。

normal.en: If a food does not agree with you, it simply does not suit your body.
normal.cn: 如果某种食物 does not agree with you，那就是它不合你的身体。

normal.en: Agree to disagree is a polite way to stop arguing without changing anyone's mind.
normal.cn: agree to disagree 是礼貌地停止争论、却不改变任何人想法的说法。

abstract.en: Picture two hands reaching in from opposite sides and closing on the same spot.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手从相反方向伸来，在同一处握在一起。

abstract.en: The hands can close on an opinion, on a price, on a set of figures, or on a verb and its subject.
abstract.cn: 这两只手可以握在一项看法上、一个价格上、一组数据上，也可以握在动词与主语之间。

abstract.en: If one hand refuses to reach, the prefix dis- appears and the grip never forms.
abstract.cn: 如果有一只手不肯伸来，否定前缀 dis- 就出现，那一握始终没有形成。

examples.en: I agree with you that the plan needs more time.
examples.cn: 我同意你的看法，这个计划需要更多时间。

examples.en: After two hours of argument, both sides agreed on a new date for the meeting.
examples.cn: 争论两小时后，双方就新的会议日期达成了一致。

examples.en: His story does not agree with the times on the ticket.
examples.cn: 他的说法与票上的时间对不上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额，哥瑞」——哥俩一个点头：同意

root: 拉丁语 gratus「令人愉快的」加前缀 ad-「向」在俗拉丁语中表示「对某人合意」，经古法语 agreer「使愉快、乐于接受」进入英语；由「合意」依次发展出同意、答应、商定、相符、适合与语法一致等义。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses all describe two things fitting together: two opinions, a person and a proposal, two negotiating sides, two accounts, food and a body, and a verb with its subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都在描述两样东西彼此相合：两种看法、一个人与一项提议、谈判双方、两份说法、食物与身体，以及动词与主语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands reach in from opposite sides and close on the same spot.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手从相反方向伸来，在同一处握在一起。

branches.en: THE OPINION: two minds find the same view pleasing and therefore hold it together.
branches.cn: 看法线：两颗心对同一个观点都觉得合意，于是共同持有它。

branches.en: THE YES: the proposal suits the person, and the person says so.
branches.cn: 应允线：提议合某人的意，这个人便把它说出来。

branches.en: THE DEAL: both sides are pleased with the same terms, which then become settled.
branches.cn: 商定线：双方对同样的条件都满意，这些条件于是定下来。

branches.en: THE FIT: records and grammatical forms must suit each other to count as correct.
branches.cn: 相符线：记录与语法形式必须彼此相合才算正确。

branches.en: THE BODY: food or climate either suits a person or does not.
branches.cn: 身体线：食物或气候要么合某人的身体，要么不合。

intro.en: Agree is a Latin-stem verb that arrived through French; English then built its nouns and adjectives with ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: agree 是经法语传入的拉丁词干动词，英语随后用普通后缀构造它的名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Gratus is a recorded Latin adjective, and ad- is a recorded prefix, so no reconstructed form is needed.
latinIntro.cn: gratus 是有记录的拉丁形容词，ad- 也是既有前缀，此处无需重构形式。

items.example: It points the pleasing towards a person.
Gratus also gives grateful and gratitude.
items.exampleCN: gratus 还生出 grateful 与 gratitude。

items.example: Old French is the direct route into English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语是进入英语的直接路径。

items.example: It forms agreement.
It forms agreeable.
It forms disagree.
It forms agreeably.

items.meaningCN: 接受彼此保留不同看法
items.example: They agreed to disagree and moved on.
items.exampleCN: 他们同意各自保留意见，继续往下谈。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「协议；一致」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「令人愉快的」

definition_zh: 协议；同意；一致；语法呼应
definition_en: a formal arrangement between people or groups, or the state of sharing the same opinion
core_image: 两份文件并排放在桌上，签名处各落一笔，笔画正好对上
scene: 长桌两端坐着两方代表，谈了很久，最后起身交换签好的文件。Both companies finally signed an agreement after months of talks.
sceneCN: 这里 agreement 是「协议、合同」（第 1 个义项：双方正式达成的约定）；句意为经过数月谈判，两家公司终于签署了一份协议。

pos.zh: 名词：协议；同意；一致；语法呼应

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀得到的基础动词，义为「同意；一致」
由基础动词加后缀 -able 构成，义为「令人愉快的；可接受的」
由否定前缀 dis- 加本词构成，义为「分歧；不一致」

senses.title: A formal arrangement between parties
senses.definition: a formal arrangement that two or more parties accept, often written and signed
senses.definitionCN: 两方或多方接受的正规安排，通常写成文字并签署
senses.example: Both companies finally signed an agreement after months of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 经过数月谈判，两家公司终于签署了一份协议。
senses.why: When two sides find the same terms pleasing, those terms harden into a document, and the document takes the name of the harmony itself.
senses.whyCN: 当双方对同样的条件都满意，这些条件就固定成一份文件，而这份文件沿用了「和谐」这个名字。

senses.title: The act of consenting
senses.definition: the fact of agreeing to something, often used without a plural
senses.definitionCN: 对某事表示同意这一事实，通常不用复数
senses.example: She nodded in agreement with the proposal.
senses.exampleCN: 她点头赞同这项提议。
senses.why: This is the abstract side of the word: the moment of consent, before anything is written down.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词抽象的一面：写下来之前那一刻的应允。

senses.title: A state of harmony
senses.definition: a situation in which people share the same view or act in harmony
senses.definitionCN: 人们持相同看法或行动协调的状态
senses.example: There is broad agreement among scientists about the cause.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家对成因有广泛共识。
senses.why: Take away the document and the handshake, and what remains is a group of minds pointing the same way.
senses.whyCN: 把文件和握手都拿掉，剩下的就是一群人的想法指向同一处。

senses.title: Matching between grammatical forms
senses.definition: the matching of words in number, person, or gender within a sentence
senses.definitionCN: 句子内部各词在数、人称或性上的相互对应
senses.example: The teacher marked every mistake in subject-verb agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把每一处主谓不一致的错误都标了出来。
senses.why: Grammar reused the everyday notion of two things fitting together for forms that must correspond.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了日常「两物相合」的观念，用来指必须相互对应的形式。

intro.en: Agreement is the noun built on agree, whose Latin root meant pleasing.
intro.cn: agreement 是在 agree 之上构成的名词，其拉丁词根意为「令人愉快的」。

items.en: Gratus meant pleasing or thankful, and it lies behind agree, grateful and gratitude.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gratus 意为「令人愉快的、感激的」，agree、grateful 与 gratitude 都出自它。

items.en: Agreer meant to please or to consent, and English borrowed it as the verb agree.
items.cn: agreer 意为「使愉快、同意」，英语借入为动词 agree。

items.en: The verb settled in English in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries with the senses of consent and harmony.
items.cn: 这个动词在十四、十五世纪稳定为英语用法，带有「同意」与「和谐」两义。

items.en: The noun agreement was formed with the suffix -ment and first named the state of being of one mind. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 名词 agreement 用后缀 -ment 构成，最早指意见一致的状态。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The written sense grew alongside commerce and law, so agreement now often means the signed document itself.
items.cn: 书面义随商业与法律一同成长，如今 agreement 常直接指那份签好的文件。

note.en: The look-alike group is the agree family; the near-meaning group gathers documents and states of consent.
note.cn: 形近组是 agree 词族；近义组收各类文件与同意的状态。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to share an opinion or to consent.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同意、意见一致」，是名词的基础形式。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning pleasant or willing to accept.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人愉快的、愿意接受的」，与 agreement 同族。

entries.definition: The opposite noun, meaning a difference of opinion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「分歧、不一致」，由否定前缀加本词构成。

entries.definition: An informal arrangement between two sides, often about business or politics.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「交易、约定」，语气较口语，多用于商务或政治。

entries.definition: A legally binding written agreement that a court can enforce.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「合同」，指具有法律约束力、可由法院强制执行的书面协议。

entries.definition: General agreement among a group, with no document involved.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「共识」，指群体内大体一致的看法，不涉及文件。

entries.definition: A formal written agreement between countries.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「条约」，专指国家之间的正式书面协定。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the agree family and the phrases agreement appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用 agree 词族，以及 agreement 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Agreement is agree plus -ment: the thing that consent leaves behind.
normal.cn: agreement 是 agree 加 -ment：同意之后留下的那件东西。

normal.en: Reach an agreement means arrive at the same point from different starting places.
normal.cn: reach an agreement 意为从不同起点走到同一个点。

normal.en: In agreement describes people, not paper: no signature is needed.
normal.cn: in agreement 描述的是人而不是纸：不需要签名。

normal.en: A trade agreement is a written deal between countries about goods.
normal.cn: trade agreement 是国家之间关于商品往来的书面协定。

normal.en: Subject-verb agreement is grammar borrowing the same idea of two things matching.
normal.cn: subject-verb agreement 是语法借用同一个「两物相合」的观念。

abstract.en: Picture two signed pages laid side by side, the strokes of the signatures meeting in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象两页签好的纸并排放在一起，两处签名笔画在中间相接。

abstract.en: Remove the pages and what is left is two minds facing the same direction.
abstract.cn: 把纸拿掉，剩下的就是两颗朝向同一方向的心。

abstract.en: Shrink the scene to one sentence and it becomes a verb matching its subject.
abstract.cn: 把场景缩小到一个句子，它就变成动词与主语的相互对应。

examples.en: Both companies finally signed an agreement after months of talks.
examples.cn: 经过数月谈判，两家公司终于签署了一份协议。

examples.en: There is broad agreement among scientists about the cause.
examples.cn: 科学家对成因有广泛共识。

examples.en: The teacher marked every mistake in subject-verb agreement.
examples.cn: 老师把每一处主谓不一致的错误都标了出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额，哥瑞门特」——哥俩一起签下门内之约：协议

root: 拉丁语 gratus「令人愉快的」经古法语 agreer「使愉快、同意」进入英语作动词 agree，再由 agree 加名词后缀 -ment 构成 agreement；由「意见一致」扩展为「协议文件」，并在语法中表示形式上的相互对应。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses move from the signed page to the moment of consent, then to a group's shared view, and finally to words agreeing inside a sentence.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项从签好的纸页，退到应允的那一刻，再到一群人共同的看法，最后落到句子里相互呼应的词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two signed pages lie side by side, and the strokes of the two signatures meet.
core.cn: 核心意象：两页签好的纸并排而放，两个签名的笔画相接。

branches.en: THE MOMENT: consent happens before anything is written, and the noun can still name it.
branches.cn: 瞬间线：应允发生在写字之前，名词仍可以指这一刻。

branches.en: THE GROUP: many minds pointing the same way form a state of harmony.
branches.cn: 群体线：许多想法指向同一处，构成一致的状态。

branches.en: THE PAGE: the harmony hardens into a signed document with terms.
branches.cn: 纸页线：和谐固化成一份写了条件的签署文件。

branches.en: THE LAW: once signed, the arrangement can be enforced, so agreement becomes a legal object.
branches.cn: 法律线：一经签署，约定便可被强制执行，于是 agreement 成为法律对象。

branches.en: THE SENTENCE: two words must fit together, which is harmony on a very small scale.
branches.cn: 句子线：两个词必须彼此相合，这是极小尺度上的和谐。

intro.en: Agreement is an English noun on a Latin-stem verb; -ment is the suffix that turns the act into a thing.
intro.cn: agreement 是建立在拉丁词干动词之上的英语名词；-ment 是把动作变成事物的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Gratus is recorded Latin, so only the deeper Indo-European origin remains uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: gratus 是有记录的拉丁词，只有更早的印欧来源仍不确定。

items.example: The root also gives grateful.
The French verb is the route into English.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语动词是进入英语的路径。

items.example: It turns agree into agreement.
items.exampleCN: 它把 agree 变成 agreement。

items.example: It forms agreeable.
It forms disagreement.
It forms the related noun employee pattern.
items.exampleCN: 它构成同类型的受动者名词。

items.example: They signed a trade agreement last spring.
items.exampleCN: 他们去年春天签署了一份贸易协定。

items.example: The two reports are in agreement.
items.exampleCN: 这两份报告的说法一致。
